I checked the Mathlib inner-product API (`norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_real`, `norm_add_eq_sqrt_iff_real_inner_eq_zero`) for existing helpers. I found none that replaces these blocks. I did not look at the `_sub` vector variants as a finding. They are thin `sub_eq_add_neg` wrappers over the `_add` lemmas, and the rubric excludes those. The replacement proofs are sketches I have not compiled. The `h0` rewriting in the second finding is only partly shared, because each theorem's disjunction has a different shape.

findings.problem: Fifteen theorems (lines 348, 356, 365, 374, 383, 391, 400, 408, 417, 426, 435, 444, 454, 464, 474) open with the same six-step rewrite chain. It turns `∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2` into `⟪p₂ -ᵥ p₃, p₁ -ᵥ p₂⟫ = 0`, the orthogonality hypothesis of the vector lemmas. The same goal-side conversion `rw [angle, ← vsub_add_vsub_cancel p₁ p₂ p₃, add_comm]` is also repeated 15 times. It rewrites `∠ p₂ p₃ p₁` as `angle x (x + y)` with `x = p₂ -ᵥ p₃`, `y = p₁ -ᵥ p₂`. The chain depends on the exact order of `neg_eq_zero`, `inner_neg_left` and `neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev`, so it is fragile. A reader has to re-derive that it always produces the same hypothesis. This is the whole point-to-vector bridge, repeated verbatim instead of stated once.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two lemmas in the `EuclideanGeometry` section:

```lean
theorem inner_vsub_vsub_eq_zero_of_angle_eq_pi_div_two {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P}
    (h : ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = π / 2) : ⟪p₂ -ᵥ p₃, p₁ -ᵥ p₂⟫ = 0 := by
  rw [angle, ← inner_eq_zero_iff_angle_eq_pi_div_two, real_inner_comm, ← neg_eq_zero, ←
    inner_neg_left, neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev] at h
  exact h

theorem angle_eq_angle_vsub_vsub_add (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) :
    ∠ p₂ p₃ p₁ = angle (p₂ -ᵥ p₃) ((p₂ -ᵥ p₃) + (p₁ -ᵥ p₂)) := by
  rw [angle, ← vsub_add_vsub_cancel p₁ p₂ p₃, add_comm]
```

The first lemma is the existing `rw ... at h` chain. The second is the existing goal rewrite. Both could be `private`.

Use 1: `angle_eq_arccos_of_angle_eq_pi_div_two` becomes
`rw [angle_eq_angle_vsub_vsub_add, dist_eq_norm_vsub' V p₃ p₂, dist_eq_norm_vsub V p₁ p₃, ← vsub_add_vsub_cancel p₁ p₂ p₃, add_comm]; exact angle_add_eq_arccos_of_inner_eq_zero (inner_vsub_vsub_eq_zero_of_angle_eq_pi_div_two h)`.
The `dist` rewrites stay, because they depend on the particular theorem.

Use 2: `angle_le_pi_div_two_of_angle_eq_pi_div_two` becomes
`rw [angle_eq_angle_vsub_vsub_add]; exact angle_add_le_pi_div_two_of_inner_eq_zero (inner_vsub_vsub_eq_zero_of_angle_eq_pi_div_two h)`.

The other 13 theorems follow the same pattern. Their `h0` conversions stay local.
findings.benefit: This removes about 15 copies of a fragile six-rewrite preamble and 15 copies of the vector-decomposition rewrite. The conversion from point angles to the vector lemmas gets a name and one place to maintain. Each geometric theorem then reads as 'apply the vector lemma', and a change to the vector API means editing one lemma, not fifteen proofs.

findings.problem: The same positivity argument for the squared hypotenuse, `0 < ‖x‖ * ‖x‖ + ‖y‖ * ‖y‖` when `x ≠ 0 ∨ y ≠ 0`, is rebuilt by hand four times. It is in `hxy` of `angle_add_eq_arcsin_of_inner_eq_zero` (lines 74–83) and in `sin_angle_add_mul_norm_of_inner_eq_zero` (lines 165–171). Each of these does a case split with `Left.add_pos_of_pos_of_nonneg`/`Left.add_pos_of_nonneg_of_pos`, `mul_self_pos` and `norm_ne_zero_iff`. The `x ≠ 0` special case is rebuilt in `angle_add_pos_of_inner_eq_zero` (lines 103–105) and `angle_add_lt_pi_div_two_of_inner_eq_zero` (lines 118–120). Each copy is long and hard to read, and each repeats the same `mul_self_pos.2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 _)` plumbing.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private lemma, which needs no inner-product hypothesis:

```lean
private theorem norm_mul_self_add_norm_mul_self_pos {x y : V} (h0 : x ≠ 0 ∨ y ≠ 0) :
    0 < ‖x‖ * ‖x‖ + ‖y‖ * ‖y‖ := by
  rcases h0 with h0 | h0
  · exact Left.add_pos_of_pos_of_nonneg (mul_self_pos.2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 h0)) (mul_self_nonneg _)
  · exact Left.add_pos_of_nonneg_of_pos (mul_self_nonneg _) (mul_self_pos.2 (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 h0))
```

Then the four uses shrink:
- `hxy` becomes `rw [pow_two, norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_real h]; exact (norm_mul_self_add_norm_mul_self_pos h0).ne'`.
- In `sin_angle_add_mul_norm_of_inner_eq_zero`, the tail after `rw [← mul_self_ne_zero, norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_real h]` becomes `exact (norm_mul_self_add_norm_mul_self_pos h0).ne'`.
- In `angle_add_pos_of_inner_eq_zero`, the argument to `Real.sqrt_pos.2` becomes `norm_mul_self_add_norm_mul_self_pos (Or.inl hx)`.
- In `angle_add_lt_pi_div_two_of_inner_eq_zero`, the argument to `Real.sqrt_pos.2` becomes `norm_mul_self_add_norm_mul_self_pos (Or.inl h0)`.
findings.benefit: The four copies of the case split and `mul_self_pos`/`norm_ne_zero_iff` plumbing become one short lemma. The proofs of the four theorems then show their trigonometric content and not the positivity bookkeeping. Any later change to this nondegeneracy argument is made once.
